hunks.header: @@ -125,7 +125,7 @@ Group `summary` is one sentence saying what the group is, describing how its hun

lines.text: - `part` is a short name (a few words) for one independent story, the same on every group in that story; the UI colors shared parts together. One document `parts[]` entry per name.

- Mechanical work (import reordering, identifier-only renames, generated code, formatting, pure moves) is its own group that keeps every hunk as refs, risk visible rather than folded into a file list. Read the old and new generated files. The summary tells the reader what they can skip and why that is safe: a pure move, an identical copy, or regenerated output that means the same (only key order or formatting, plus the one real change if there is one). An identical copy of a file in the diff sits with its source. That group's summary still says the copy is identical. When it exists only because of a story, it is that part's last group with nothing depending on it. When it could have been its own PR, it is its own part.
- `suggestedOrder` walks the whole review, independent parts included. Mechanical parts, independent documentation, and test-only cleanup go last.

- Document `size` is human review burden: `trivial`, `small`, `medium`, `large`, `very-large`. Forty files changing one import in one group are `small`; three files rewriting a contract the rest of the system hangs on can be `large`.

- Document `size` is human review burden: `trivial`, `small`, `medium`, `large`, `very-large`. Forty files changing one import in one group are `small`. A new contract that the checks, the UI, and the instructions all use is `large`. Merging those layers into fewer groups keeps that `size`.

- Coverage: every live hunk sits in at least one group. A path covers every live hunk of that file. Duplicate refs across groups are allowed. Unreferenced hunks fail `validate` and show as Unassigned in the UI.
- Lockfiles have no hunk refs; the CLI leaves them out of the skeleton and the UI gives them their own closed bucket. Hunk refs exist only for hunks the skeleton lists.

- A path stays valid when a rebase only shifts line numbers. `path@oldStart+newStart` goes stale when those starts move, and that fails `validate`. `serve` still starts, shows git at those SHAs, and flags the broken pointer. Re-run `review` and copy fresh paths. A dirty work tree does not make refs stale.
